source_text:
Οἱ οὐρανοὶ τῇ διοικήσει αὐτοῦ σαλευόμενοι ἐν εἰρήνῃ ὑποτάσσονται αὐτῷ.
ἡμέρα τε καὶ νὺξ τὸν τεταγμένον ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δρόμον διανύουσιν, μηδὲν ἀλλήλοις ἐμποδίζοντα.
ἥλιός τε καὶ σελήνη, ἀστέρων τε χοροὶ κατὰ τὴν διαταγὴν αὐτοῦ ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ δίχα πάσης παρεκβάσεως ἐξελίσσουσιν τοὺς ἐπιτεταγμένους αὐτοῖς ὁρισμούς.
γῆ κυοφοροῦσα κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ τοῖς ἰδίοις καιροῖς τὴν πανπληθῆ ἀνθρώποις τε καὶ θηρσὶν καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ζώοις ἀνατέλλει τροφήν, μὴ διχοστατοῦσα μηδὲ ἀλλοιοῦσά τι τῶν δεδογματισμένων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.
ἀβύσσων τε ἀνεξιχνίαστα καὶ νερτέρων ἀνεκδιήγητα κλίματα τοῖς αὐτοῖς συνέχεται προστάγμασιν.
τὸ κύτος τῆς ἀπείρου θαλάσσης κατὰ τὴν δημιουργίαν αὐτοῦ συσταθὲν εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς οὐ παρεκβαίνει τὰ περιτεθειμένα αὐτῇ κλεῖθρα, ἀλλὰ καθὼς διέταξεν αὐτῇ, οὕτως ποιεῖ.
εἶπεν γάρ: Ἕως ὧδε ἥξεις, καὶ τὰ κύματά σου ἐν σοὶ συντριβήσεται.
ὠκεανὸς ἀπέραντος ἀνθρώποις καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτὸν κόσμοι ταῖς αὐταῖς ταγαῖς τοῦ δεσπότου διευθύνονται.
καιροὶ ἐαρινοὶ καὶ θερινοὶ καὶ μετοπωρινοὶ καὶ χειμερινοὶ ἐν εἰρήνῃ μεταπαραδιδόασιν ἀλλήλοις.
ἀνέμων σταθμοὶ κατὰ τὸν ἴδιον καιρὸν τὴν λειτουργίαν αὐτῶν ἀπροσκόπως ἐπιτελοῦσιν: ἀέναοί τε πηγαί, πρὸς ἀπόλαυσιν καὶ ὑγείαν δημιουργηθεῖσαι, δίχα ἐλλείψεως παρέχονται τοὺς πρὸς ζωῆς ἀνθρώποις μαζούς: τά τε ἐλάχιστα τῶν ζώων τὰς συνελεύσεις αὐτῶν ἐν ὁμονοίᾳ καὶ εἰρήνῃ ποιοῦνται.
ταῦτα πάντα ὁ μέγας δημιουργὸς καὶ δεσπότης τῶν ἁπάντων ἐν εἰρήνῃ καὶ ὁμονοίᾳ προσέταξεν εἶναι, εὐεργετῶν τὰ πάντα, ὑπερεκπερισσῶς δὲ ἡμᾶς τοὺς προσπεφευγότας τοῖς οἰκτιρμοῖς αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ μεγαλωσύνη εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
orientation: The Roman church is describing how all parts of creation obey God's ordered will in peace and harmony, as a model for the Corinthians.
pass_a_gloss: The heavens, being shaken by his governance, submit to him in peace. Day and night complete the course ordered by him, hindering one another in nothing. Sun and moon, and the choirs of stars, according to his command, in harmony without any deviation, roll through the bounds assigned to them. Earth, conceiving according to his will, at its own seasons brings forth abundant food for humans and beasts and all the living creatures that are on it, not dissenting nor altering any of the things decreed by him. The unsearchable things of the deeps and the indescribable regions of the netherworld are held together by the same ordinances. The hollow of the boundless sea, established according to his creation into its gatherings, does not transgress the bars placed around it, but as he commanded it, so it does. For he said: 'As far as this you shall come, and your waves shall be broken within you.' The ocean impassable to humans and the worlds beyond it are directed by the same orders of the master. Spring and summer and autumn and winter seasons pass over to one another in peace. The stations of the winds at their own season complete their ministry without stumbling; and the ever-flowing springs, created for enjoyment and health, without deficiency offer their breasts for the life of humans; and the smallest of living creatures make their gatherings in harmony and peace. All these things the great creator and master of all things commanded to be in peace and harmony, doing good to all things, and superabundantly to us who have fled for refuge to his mercies through our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory and the majesty forever and ever. Amen.

choices.why: The glossary requires 'harmony' for ὁμόνοια, and the phrase is central to the section's argument that creation models the harmony the Corinthians lack.
Peace is the other key term paired with harmony throughout this section, and the plain English 'peace' preserves the contrast with the Corinthians' faction.
The glossary requires 'ministry' for λειτουργία, and here the winds' ordered service mirrors the ordered ministry the letter defends.

choices.english: who have fled for refuge to his mercies
choices.why: The perfect participle conveys a completed act of taking refuge, and 'mercies' preserves the plural of οἰκτιρμοῖς, which is theologically significant in early Christian language.
rejected: who have taken refuge in his mercies

choices.why: The passive perfect participle 'placed around' keeps the sense that God set the sea's limits, and 'bars' is the concrete image of the boundary.
The compound adverb intensifies the contrast between God's general beneficence and his special favor to believers; 'superabundantly' captures the emphatic prefix.

bible_refs.note: Ἕως ὧδε ἥξεις, καὶ τὰ κύματά σου ἐν σοὶ συντριβήσεται

pass_b_english: The heavens move at his direction and submit to him in peace.
Day and night complete the course he has set for them, and neither hinders the other.
Sun and moon and the choirs of stars roll through the boundaries he has assigned them in harmony, without any deviation.

The earth conceives according to his will and in its own seasons brings forth food for the teeming multitude of humans and beasts and all the living creatures on it. It does not dissent from anything he has decreed, nor alter it.
The unsearchable depths of the abysses and the indescribable regions of the underworld are held together by the same commands.
The vast expanse of the boundless sea was gathered together by his creative work into its reservoirs. It does not transgress the bars placed around it, but does just as he commanded it.
For he said, “Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you” (Job 38:11).
The ocean, impassable to humans, and the worlds beyond it are directed by the same ordinances of the Master.
Spring and summer and autumn and winter pass into one another in peace.
The stations of the winds perform their ministry at their proper time without stumbling.
The ever-flowing springs, created for enjoyment and health, offer their breasts for human life without fail.
Even the smallest of living creatures make their gatherings in harmony and peace.

All these things the great Creator and Master of all things commanded to exist in peace and harmony. He does good to all things, and superabundantly to us who have fled for refuge to his mercies through our Lord Jesus Christ,
to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever. Amen.

polish.changed: Broke long sentences into shorter, clearer units; made implied subjects explicit where needed; kept every claim and Scripture reference intact while improving natural English rhythm for reading aloud.

last_rejected.why: μαζοί means 'breasts' but context demands 'streams' or 'flow'—springs don't have breasts; false friend with μαστός.
last_rejected.ruling: μαζός means 'breast' in LSJ; poetic metaphor for springs offering breasts is standard, not a false friend.

last_rejected.quote: brings forth food for the teeming multitude of humans and beasts and all the living creatures on it
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν πανπληθῆ ἀνθρώποις τε καὶ θηρσὶν καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐπ’ αὐτῆς ζώοις ἀνατέλλει τροφήν
last_rejected.why: πανπληθῆ agrees with τροφήν: the food is abundant, not the creatures a teeming multitude.
last_rejected.fix: in its own seasons brings forth abundant food for humans and beasts and all the living creatures on it.
last_rejected.ruling: πανπληθῆ is accusative singular feminine agreeing with τροφήν ('all-abundant food'); English wrongly makes humans/beasts a 'teeming multitude', but the sense is minor, not meaning-changing.
